title: Padding and injective reductions

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §2.4 Lemma 2.12 and Theorem 2.13, p.20; §5.1 Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.5 and Exercise 5.6, pp.29–30

summary: Build distinct program indices with the same behavior, then use them to translate enumerable problems injectively into halting.
abstract: Adding an unused tag to a program can change its finite description while preserving every output and every divergence. Making that construction explicit gives infinitely many distinct names for each partial computable function, and lets a terminating calculation avoid any finite list of forbidden names. The same distinction between names and behavior strengthens computable reductions: an injective translation preserves different input questions as well as their answers. Such translations still cannot be manufactured into every target set, as a two-element set and a singleton demonstrate. For the halting problem, however, the specified program constructor already retains the requested computation and supplies injective translations of every computably enumerable membership problem and connects the usual halting conventions.
